caption: What if your skin worked like a lotus leaf? Rain would bead up and roll off you like tiny marbles, and you'd stay completely dry. On a lotus leaf, a water drop stays almost a perfect ball, with a contact angle of up to about 170°. The secret is microscopic: the leaf is covered in tiny bumps, about 10 to 20 micrometres tall, coated in wax. The drop rests on the bump tips and pockets of air, so only about 0.6% of it touches the leaf. As drops roll off, they pick up dust and dirt. That's how lotus leaves stay clean while growing in muddy ponds. Your kitchen has a cousin: arbi (taro) leaves bead water almost as well. Scientists even copied the trick to make self-cleaning wall paint that rain washes clean. Plot twist: it works because of water's strong surface tension. Oil doesn't bead up the same way, so oily samosa fingers would still leave a mark. Would YOU want lotus-leaf skin? 👇
